candidates.explanation: In the `else if (userByEmail)` branch, any existing user whose status is not inactive (including an active password/email account) gets its provider overwritten with the social provider and its socialId set, then saved via update. The check only excludes inactive users, so an active email/password account is taken over by Google. After that, the email login sees provider 'google' and refuses with 'needLoginViaProvider'. The code should not change the provider of an existing active email account (or should require explicit linking/authentication).

fix.description: In the `else if (userByEmail)` branch, do not overwrite provider/socialId on an existing account that is not already a social account. Reject the login with an error (e.g. emailAlreadyExists / needLoginViaProvider with provider 'email') or require explicit account linking, instead of calling usersService.update with provider = authProvider. Only allow adoption when the existing account is inactive, or already uses the same social provider.
